c0: Every large enterprise gets assets back: end-of-lease equipment, returns, retired fleet, surplus. Each one is a decision worth money. This is Circularity, the agentic decision layer that makes it.
c1a: An executive doesn't start with dashboards. They start with a briefing: two point four million dollars recovered, one point seven million of new purchases avoided, and where value is at risk right now, with its owner.
c1b: Every answer shows the tools the agent called, so no number is taken on trust.
c2: Your systems already run every step of a return: the contract, the authorisation, the transport, the receipt, the inspection. None of them decides the asset's best next life across all of that evidence. Circularity sits at exactly that moment, and hands the work back to the systems you run.
c3a: For the planner, the agent has already prepared twenty-one decisions, and ranked what needs a person.
c3b: One returned motor. Seven possible next lives, compared on one economic basis. Redeploying it against a customer's replacement order is worth ninety-six hundred dollars, forty-eight hundred more than selling it, with a range, not a guess. One route is ruled out before price is even considered: there is no confirmed buyer, so the gate excludes it.
c3c: Ask it why. It calls the rules, the prediction models, and the evidence, each one labelled retrieved, model, or rules. And it drafts the rationale for you.
c3d: It already shows what will be sent where, once it's approved. The planner submits. Agents prepare. People commit.
c4a: The approver sees the drafted rationale, their own approval limit, and the exact instruction, before anything leaves. Your systems stay authoritative for the work.
c4b: One approval reference travels with every instruction. There is no auto-approve path.
c5a: Behind the screen, every stage of this asset's journey was run by Circularity's agents. Each line shows the agent, the tool it called, the system it reached, what it got, and the audit I D that proves it.
c5b: Where models come into play, it names them. A vision model checks the inspection photos against the inspector's grade, and a survival model estimates the remaining life.
c5c: The Opportunity Finder matches demand, prices every route with gradient-boosted models, and decides. Each model shows its measured error, so you know how far to trust it.
c5d: The Handoff Coordinator sends the approved plan into your order, maintenance and warehouse processes, and each one sends its own reference back. Then the actual result comes back on its own.
c5e: Finance confirms the outcome, and the Reconciler and the Analytics Explainer close the loop.
c6a: Circularity connects to what you already run: lease, E R P, asset management, repair, warehouse, service, quality and market data. Those systems keep owning their transactions.
c6b: And it's open by design. Circularity uses your platforms' agent tools, and your own agents can call its governed tools. Every agent has a scope it cannot exceed.
c7: Measured against current practice: thirty-seven percent more value recovered, one point seven million of spend avoided, and value realised twenty-two percent faster.
c8: Start in shadow mode, beside your teams. Then one route, then the closed loop, then the whole portfolio. Your systems run the work. Circularity makes sure it's the right work. Agent-first, human-governed.
c4p: Now the approver: the person with the authority to commit.
c5a2: Watch the counters: agents, tool calls, model calls and audit entries. Every one of them is recorded.
c6c: And you decide how far each agent may go, role by role and action by action: off, suggest, prepare, or act and notify, with a kill switch for every agent. Commitments always stop at a person.
c7b: And because every decision is reconciled against its outcome, the forecasts get measurably better with every cycle.
c5f: Ninety-six hundred predicted, ninety-two thirty actual, explained line by line, and the model learns from the difference.
